title: 9th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened at 09:02 on 1 July 2024 with 60 members present. The Speaker offered condolences to Thulusdhoo member Ibrahim Naseem on his father's death, announced two committee seat swaps, and welcomed a school group from Milandhoo in the gallery. Members then held the first debate on the government's Fiscal Responsibility Bill, sponsored by Naseem; most speakers backed it, while debate also covered past borrowing, recurrent spending and the central bank advance clause. After a 30-minute recess the sitting moved to the debate on the Public Debt Bill, where the speakers heard in this part again supported the bill; no vote was taken in this part. The text is partly garbled, so figures quoted by speakers were not captured. This part continues the debate on the government's Public Debt Bill (item 6.1), sponsored by Funadhoo member Mohamed Mamdooh. Fourteen members spoke, all in support of the bill and several asking for it to go to committee for study; much of the debate was about the previous MDP government's borrowing and spending, and about transparency on how loans are used. No vote was recorded in this part, and the chair adjourned the sitting to give time to committee work, with the next sitting set for Tuesday 2 July 2024 at 9:00. Some of the text is garbled, so figures quoted by members may be imperfect.

items.outcome: debated; paused for recess, not concluded in this part

items.title: Continued debate on the Public Debt Bill (submitted on behalf of the government by Funadhoo member Mohamed Mamdooh)
items.outcome: debated; no vote in this part, sitting adjourned

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill as a new fiscal system replacing the 2013 law and criticised past MDP-era spending.
Raised a point of order disputing the loan figures given by the previous speaker.
Supports the bill and criticises spending on public sector investment projects and other costs under the previous government.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said MDP supports the reform agenda but argued recurrent spending rose under this government and loans fall due in 2024 to 2026.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill, saying past governments spent without regard to income and that central bank advances are common elsewhere.
Tells the public not to worry, saying the bill lets the state manage its debt; raises repairs needed and access to health services.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Backed the bill but urged the government to speed up fiscal reform, citing new embassies, a development bank and state company hiring.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Raised a point of order that a speaker had strayed from the bill (not accepted by the chair).
Supported the bill as curbing wasteful spending and called for the central bank governor to answer to the Majlis.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the Fiscal Responsibility Bill and said the money-printing concern is answered by its rules.
Supported the Public Debt Bill, arguing debt rose sharply without accountability and needs a clear framework.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the bill and compared MDP-era and current government spending for January to June.
Raised a point of order saying the figures he gave covered January to June only.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the bill and said it contains no tax increase despite public talk to that effect.
Says state companies' subsidies drive debt, backs the president's price reviews for state fish buying, and calls for Aasandha reform.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Says the bill sets checks and balances on borrowing and a debt management office, and asks the committee to study it quickly so it becomes law.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Presented the bill as replacing the 2013 spending law with fiscal rules, a strategy statement and budget outcome reports; defended the central bank advance clause as a cash-flow tool.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Called the bill important for sound fiscal policy, citing low wages and past spending above budget.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill and urged quick passage; cited council foreign-trip spending as a reason for spending discipline.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the bill, saying earlier borrowing lacked clear purpose or rules and that the bill is needed to rein in spending.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill, saying fiscal policy should set clear spending principles and keep total debt within a fixed limit.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill and urged the Majlis to debate it technically rather than politically.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supported the Public Debt Bill and called for a system to investigate borrowing by past governments.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the Public Debt Bill, citing debt management practice in Australia and Malaysia and urging project prioritisation.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the Public Debt Bill and urged adding an accountability chapter involving bodies such as the Auditor General and ACC (turn continues past this part).

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supports the bill but says it is not enough alone and the debt situation must be examined; argues the debt must be managed responsibly.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Thanks the government and the sponsor; says such a bill was long needed and criticises past governments' borrowing and asset sales.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: As sponsor, says the bill shows the government's sincerity on debt and criticises borrowing and spending under the previous MDP government.

speakers.name: Asadhulla Shihab
positions: Thanks the sponsor and criticises the previous government's money printing and handling of state companies, presenting the bill as a remedy.

speakers.name: Hassan Waheed
positions: Supports the bill, noting it covers debt management by local councils and aims to stop past borrowing practices recurring.

speakers.name: Mohamed Afoo Hamid
positions: Supports the bill and praises the government's work on strengthening the financial system.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Supports the bill; says laws must be enforced and that unpaid taxes and rent owed to the state by resort owners should be collected.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Supports the bill but criticises current spending and political appointments; wants the committee to make all borrowers accountable.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supports the bill as a way to show citizens how loans are spent, and questions what past loans delivered.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Supports the bill and says the former finance minister should be summoned to explain the loans taken under the previous government.

decisions: Committee changes announced: Kaashidhoo member Munthazim Ibrahim replaces Kurendhoo member Mohamed Shamin Habeeb on the public safety services committee, and the two swap on the economic committee.
The chair extended condolences to Thulusdhoo member Ibrahim Naseem on his father's death.
The chair did not accept three points of order (from the Velidhoo, South Feydhoo and Baarashu members) as valid points of order.
Debate on the Fiscal Responsibility Bill paused for a recess from 10:33 to 11:01 and the sitting moved to item 6.1.
The chair adjusted the speaking order so members due at committee meetings spoke first.
The chair adjourned the sitting to leave time for committee work.
The next sitting was set for Tuesday 2 July 2024 at 9:00.
